title: Subsets II
prompt:
Given an integer array that **may contain duplicates**, return all possible subsets with no duplicate subsets in the result, in any order.

**Example**: `[1,2,2]` → `[[],[1],[1,2],[1,2,2],[2],[2,2]]`.

**Constraints**: 1 ≤ n ≤ 10.
hints: Two equal values create identical branches in the recursion tree. What can you do to the input so duplicates are easy to spot?
Sort `nums`, then use the Subsets template: record at every call, loop from `start`, recurse with `i + 1`.
Skip repeated values in the same loop: `if (i > start && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;`. The first copy in each loop still recurses.

solution.explanation: After sorting, equal values sit next to each other. The `i > start` check skips a value only when it repeats one already tried in the same loop, where it would start an identical branch. Going deeper can still pick the next copy, so `[2,2]` is reachable. O(n·2ⁿ) time worst case, O(n) recursion depth.
